source.job: Author the five withheld recoveries, attached to their existing CORE scenes (2026-08-31). The attachment points were sited by the CORE compulsory-set audit and are machine-readable as A1001-A1006 in proposed/core-recovery-attachments-2026-08-31.json; this file is the commissioned authoring of the five that attach. A1004 (M3, the mid-story challenge) is deliberately absent — it cannot attach without giving CORE a story turn it does not have, and it lives on the every-optional-walk floor instead.
source.statement: AUTHORED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. Every continuation line in this file was written for its scene against the sited attachment point. There is no corpus behind the continuations: no `row` appears anywhere and no continuation line is attested speech. Where a walk restages the canonical turn it attaches to, that turn is a QUOTATION of walks/pod-0.json's transcription — marked `restaged: true`, carrying no row field — and contributes nothing to any corpus accounting. The transcription itself lives only in walks/pod-0.json.

format: A walk is a sequence of NODE REFERENCES. Each step names a node and a position; the surface sentence is a property of the step, never the step itself. Copied from walks/pod-0.json so coverage stays computable without parsing prose.

register.note: CORE recoveries in CORE's own worlds: a seat on the bus into town, a café counter, a street arrangement between friends, a first conversation. Every one of these exists in every pair a course ships to; nothing here is Wales, nothing is a sector. English is the canonical known text and is pair-invariant; where the canon writes a [target language] bracket, this file renders it deictically ('your language'), per the scene 0 convention, so the pair overlay may substitute names on the target side.
register.casts: Inherited, none invented: Sarah and the Passenger (pod-0 W3), Sarah and the Barista (pod-0 W1), Sarah and the Friend (pod-0 W4), the Learner and the Friend (pod-0 W16).

attachment.policy: A RECOVERY ATTACHES, IT DOES NOT APPEND (Tom's ruling, 2026-08-31): a pod is a branch point with its continuations attached, so each recovery is the other half of a move CORE already teaches, and hangs off the scene that exists. CORE's existing order is untouched — walks/pod-0.json is not modified and nothing is reordered. Each walk here names the pod-0 walk and step it attaches to, restages that turn as a quotation, and continues it inside the same encounter. A recovery three scenes later would be worth nothing; every one of these arrives while the learner is in the trouble the branch just made.

accounting.corpus_rows_note: Zero, and that is the point: nothing here is a transcription. The restaged turns are quotations of pod-0 rows and are counted only in walks/pod-0.json.

walks.W1301: S2 (A1001) — the hedge acted on and turned out wrong, scene 2, attached at pod-0 W3 step 4
walks.W1302: M1 (A1002) — 'I don't know', held with status, the third arm on the canon's one stored branch, scene 3, attached at pod-0 W1 step 4
walks.W1303: M5 (A1006) — the haggle over WHEN, settled by formula, scene 4, attached at pod-0 W4 step 3

coverage_of_the_graph.note: S2 is the only corpus-attested edge with no recovery anywhere in the estate — five hedges attested, not one ever taken up; W1301 is its first. M1's recovery gives O2 ('nobody knows') its first dialogic home in CORE: the canon's recorded property is that nobody in it ever fails, and W1302 is the first turn in CORE where a responder does not know the answer. M5's recovery runs N16's four positions inside N7's arrangement — the one register where everyone haggles honestly — and the price-haggle is explicitly NOT attached, per the audit; no ratified composition edge exists for N16-inside-N7, so the composition is carried per-step and not cited as a C-edge.

walks.name: Scene 2 — the hedge acted on, and the sign that corrects it (S2)
walks.note: The bus into town, pod-0 W3's world, the morning of the day of greetings. The canon's hedge — 'maybe three or four miles' — is attested five times and taken up never; this walk takes it up. The shape the learner owns when it ends: a hedge is a licence to act plus a licence to be wrong. The hedge propagates into the plan ('I might get off'), the world supplies the correction — a road sign, never a mood — and the recovery is that nobody promised, so nobody is owed an apology. The passenger's last line hands over certainty where certainty genuinely exists: the estimate was hedged, the last stop is not.

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.surface: Can you tell me how far it is into town?
steps.note: Quotation of the canon's ticket (pod-0 W3 step 3). The seat business has already run; this walk begins where the trouble begins.

steps.speaker: Passenger
steps.surface: It's not very far. Maybe three or four miles.
steps.note: Quotation of the canon's hedge (pod-0 W3 step 4) — the exact turn S2 hangs on. In the canon no turn takes this up; everything after this step is the continuation the corpus never stored.

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.surface: Three or four miles — I could walk that. I might get off at the next stop, then, and walk the rest. It's a nice morning for it.
steps.note: The hedge acted on, out loud — and acting on an answer out loud IS a read-back, which is why this is N4's read-back position: saying the plan is what gives the world its chance to object. The hedge has propagated honestly into the plan — 'I might', not 'I will' — because a hedged answer breeds a hedged plan, and that propagation is the learner already owning half the shape.

steps.speaker: Passenger
steps.surface: Oh — hold on. There's the sign: six miles to town. It's further than I thought. I'm sorry.
steps.note: The confirm slot filled with a revision — not-that-but-this, F6. The world motivates the correction: a road sign on the way into town is exactly where a hedged distance meets ground truth mid-journey. The passenger apologises because real people do; the next turn's job is to show the apology was never owed.

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.surface: Don't be — you said maybe, and maybe was right. Six is too far for me. I'll stay in this seat and ride the whole way.
steps.note: The recovery, complete in one turn: the hedge acknowledged as having done its job — 'you said maybe, and maybe was right', nobody promised — and the re-orientation without grievance, the revised number read straight back into a revised plan. The bound read-back/confirm pair runs twice in this walk, once around the wrong number and once around the right one.

steps.speaker: Passenger
steps.surface: Do that. It's the last stop, anyway — you can't miss it.
steps.note: Confirm plus something thrown in, F2 — and the something is certainty, offered exactly where certainty exists. The passenger only ever estimated the distance, but the route's last stop is a fact; the contrast between the hedged answer and the unhedged one is the quietest lesson in the walk.

walks.name: Scene 3 — 'I don't know', held with status: the third arm at the café (M1)
walks.note: The café, pod-0 W1's world, mid-order: the coffee is already being made. The canon's one stored branch forks the crisps question into yes (g16) and no (g15); this walk is its third arm — the answer that is neither, because the barista genuinely cannot know yet: today's delivery is still in its boxes. The not-knowing is held with status — the boxes have the answer even though the barista does not — and that status is what licenses Sarah's next move: re-route the ask from the person to the means, O2's own recovery, staged transactionally. CORE trains asking, and asking summons this answer; before this walk, no responder anywhere in CORE ever failed to know anything.

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.surface: Do you have crisps, or nuts, or anything?
steps.note: Quotation of the canon's availability ticket (pod-0 W1 step 3). The coffee was ordered two turns ago and is on its way — that fact does quiet work at step 3.

steps.speaker: Barista
steps.surface: I honestly don't know — today's delivery is still in its boxes. There might be crisps in there; there might not.
steps.via_branch: the third arm — neither the canon's no (g15) nor its yes (g16)
steps.note: N13's I-don't-know, filling N3's answer slot, and the world explains why a barista can fail to know their own stock: the delivery only just arrived and nobody has opened it. The not-knowing is held WITH STATUS — the barista names exactly where the answer lives — and that is the difference between a dead end and a door. F15 with the account standing visibly in the room, boxes and all.

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.surface: Would you have a look? No rush — I'm waiting on my coffee anyway.
steps.note: The question the not-knowing licenses — N13's own third position, and O2's recovery in one turn: the ask re-routed from the person to the means. The world makes the request cheap to grant: her coffee is still being made, so the minute the boxes cost was already spoken for. A learner who owns this turn is never stranded by 'I don't know' again — they ask the question it points to.

steps.speaker: Barista
steps.surface: Right — you're in luck. Crisps, two kinds. No nuts, though.
steps.note: The deferred answer, back from the boxes: the availability ticket finally gets what the canon's branch gives it immediately, one loop later. F2 — the answer plus what was thrown in, the exact count and the honest no on the nuts. From here the walk rejoins the canon's yes branch.

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.surface: Crisps will do nicely — salted, please.
steps.note: Re-select and specify, the transaction resuming as if the loop had never happened — because to the transaction, it hadn't: the detour cost one turn each way and nothing else, which is the whole lesson.

steps.speaker: Barista
steps.surface: Here's your coffee — and your crisps.
steps.note: Delivery, echoing the canon's own g18 shape with the recovered item riding alongside. The canon's close (thanks and goodbye) follows unchanged.

walks.name: Scene 4 — the counterbid over when, settled by formula (M5)
walks.note: The street at seven in the evening, pod-0 W4's world — the corpus's only two-sided negotiation, and without knowing it the canon has already walked the haggle's first two positions: Sarah's 'tomorrow' is a number on the table (N16.1) and the friend's 'Saturday' is its counterbid (N16.2). This walk adds positions 3 and 4: the learner's counter is countered again, and the pair settle by formula — take the overlap, say it with 'then', add the precision that makes it real. O9's recovery is 'produce a third position, or yield'; Sarah's third position is Saturday morning. The whole thing stays brisk because the world demands it: Sarah opened by saying she has no time to talk, so a leisurely negotiation would contradict the scene it stands in — and the friend's last line sends her home, honouring the constraint she declared at the start. The PRICE-haggle is explicitly not attached; over money this shape belongs to enrichment, and teaching it at a UK counter would teach a false pragmatic. Over WHEN, everyone haggles honestly.

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.surface: Hello! I'm sorry but I can't talk at the moment. I need to go home now. Can we talk tomorrow?
steps.note: Quotation of the canon (pod-0 W4 step 2): decline, account, counter — and, read as a haggle, the first number on the table: tomorrow. The 'I need to go home now' is not scenery; it is the clock the whole walk runs on.

steps.speaker: Friend
steps.surface: No, I'm sorry, I'm busy tomorrow. But let's talk on Saturday. See you then.
steps.note: Quotation of the canon (pod-0 W4 step 3) — the second no, and the counterbid: Saturday. The canon ends the scene here, with the friend's 'see you then' closing the books on a settlement the learner never actually agreed to. Everything after this step is the continuation the corpus never stored: what the learner does when THEIR number has just been countered.

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.surface: Saturday's good — but only the morning. I'm away all afternoon.
steps.note: The third position, produced rather than swallowed: not a yield to Saturday-whenever, not a relitigation of tomorrow, but a narrowing with its reason attached — F5 in miniature, no-here's-why-here's-instead. Reopening a closed 'see you then' needs a real constraint, and she has one; a preference would not have earned the turn.

steps.speaker: Friend
steps.surface: Saturday morning, then. Ten o'clock, at the café?
steps.note: The settlement formula, whole: take the overlap of the two constraints, seal it with 'then', and add the precision — a time, a place — that turns an agreement into an arrangement. 'Saturday morning, then' is the exact shape the audit sited this attachment for; the learner who owns this turn can end any haggle that has an overlap left in it.

steps.speaker: Sarah
steps.surface: Ten at the café — perfect. See you Saturday!
steps.note: Accept by read-back: the time and place said back before they are sealed, the same motif the canon reserves for numbers that matter (the hotel's booking, the chemist's dosage). What gets read back is exactly what was newly minted at step 4 — the precision, not the whole negotiation.

steps.speaker: Friend
steps.surface: Go on home, then — Saturday at ten!
steps.note: The second signature on the settlement, folded into the ritual close — and the release: the friend sends Sarah home, honouring the 'I need to go home now' she opened with. The haggle cost four turns inside an encounter that had no time to spare, which is the proof it was cheap.
